{{Short description|American engineer and radio personality (1936–2018)}}
[[File:BillWattenburgPorch.png|alt=Bill Wattenburg, circa 2000.|thumb|Bill Wattenburg, {{Circa|2000}}]]
'''Willard Harvey Wattenburg''' (February 9, 1936&nbsp;– August 2, 2018)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://padailypost.com/2018/08/06/longtime-kgo-radio-host-and-scientist-bill-wattenburg-dead-at-82/|title=Longtime KGO radio host and scientist Bill Wattenburg dead at 82|date=August 6, 2018}}</ref> was an American [[inventor]], [[engineer]], [[author]], and [[Talk radio|talk radio show host]] from [[California]]. Advertisements for his show often referred to him as "The Smartest Man in the World."<ref name="KGO Web Page">{{cite web|url=http://www.kgoam810.com/sectional.asp?id=25869 |title=KGO Audio and Podcasts |access-date=2010-02-07 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111123140627/http://www.kgoam810.com/sectional.asp?id=25869 |archivedate=2011-11-23 }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born and raised in [[Greenville, California]], in rural [[Plumas County, California|Plumas County]], Wattenburg grew up working with his father in the logging business.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sfgate.com/politics/joegarofoli/article/CHRONICLE-PROFILE-Bill-Wattenburg-Radio-host-2787327.php|title=CHRONICLE PROFILE / Bill Wattenburg / Radio host keeps creative lines open / Inventor, best-selling author creates simple solutions to complex problems|newspaper=Sfgate |date=7 October 2002|publisher= |last1=Garofoli |first1=Joe }}</ref> His scientific talent was discovered by a teacher, who encouraged him to apply to several schools, including the [[University of California, Berkeley]] where he completed his first year with honors.{{citation needed|date=August 2018}} After his freshman year, Wattenburg moved back to assist his father in his business, and graduated from [[California State University, Chico]], [[Latin honors|summa cum laude]] in [[physics]] and [[electrical engineering]], in 1959.<ref name="wattenburg.us">{{cite web |title=Bill Wattenburg |url=http://www.wattenburg.us/ |website=www.wattenburg.us |access-date=25 June 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100623023024/http://www.wattenburg.us/ |archive-date=23 June 2010}}</ref> He then returned to Berkeley for his doctorate in electrical engineering, in 1962,<ref name="ieee/37086413318">{{cite web |title=Bill Wattenburg |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/author/37086413318 |website=ieeexplore.ieee.org |access-date=25 June 2025}}</ref> with professor [[Harry Huskey]], completing it in three years, and worked at the [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] and as a professor at Berkeley 1962 to 1966.<ref name="KGO">{{cite web|url=http://www.kgoam810.com/viewentry.asp?ID=336823&PT=PERSONALITIES |title=KGO 810 AM Biography |access-date=2008-05-09 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110525123300/http://www.kgoam810.com/viewentry.asp?ID=336823&PT=PERSONALITIES |archivedate=2011-05-25 }}</ref> After that, he was a consultant to various engineering and defense-oriented businesses. He remained a consultant to the Livermore Laboratory until his death.<ref name="KGO" />

== Engineering==
As an engineer, Wattenburg discovered many of the original problems with the [[Bay Area Rapid Transit]] system, including such flaws as easily decipherable fare cards (which could have fare value fraudulently added to them), trains that failed to show up on the computer screen, and other deficiencies.<ref name="Pushback web page summary of BART work">{{cite web | title = Bill Wattenburg's Background: BART&nbsp;— Bay Area Rapid Transit System | url = http://www.pushback.com/Wattenburg/bio/BART.html}}</ref> He published<ref name="sfgate/2935571">{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Michael |title=Simple Way to Clean Up Refugee Camps' Mess / Plan for buckets backed by White House |url=https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/simple-way-to-clean-up-refugee-camps-mess-plan-2935571.php |website=[[sfgate.com]] |access-date=25 June 2025 |date=April 19, 1999}}</ref> numerous articles in scientific journals and continued to do research as an adjunct professor at Cal State, Chico.

== Businessman ==
Wattenburg patented the first home alarm system using electrical wiring for its communication medium. Many of his ideas, such as using flatbed rail cars as temporary bridges,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/bridge/prefab/psbsreport03.cfm|title=2. Historical Background Of Steel Bridges - Prefabricated Steel Bridge Systems: Final Report - ABC - Accelerated - Technologies and Innovations - Construction - Federal Highway Administration|website=[[Federal Highway Administration|Federal Highway Administration (FHWA)]]}}</ref> unenergized electric water heaters for storage of emergency potable water, and converting plow blades into minesweepers are deceptively simple variants of [[prior art]] or [[folk technology]].

=== Mountaintop removal mine ===
In the 1980s Wattenburg set up his own gold mining corporation, "[[Wattexco]]". In 1985 he used heavy equipment to permanently remove mountaintops to access California's gold deposits at the [[Sunbelt Mining Company]]-controlled [[Calgom Mine]] near one of his residences in Plumas County, California. In contrast to the historic practice of [[gold panning]] in California, Wattenburg orchestrated<ref name=palmer>M.A. Palmer et al. ''Mountaintop Mining Consequences'', ''Science'', 8 January 2010, Vol. 327, p. 148.</ref> [[mountaintop removal mining]] to get at the gold beneath an entire mountain in Plumas County.

In a 1992 interview with a [[private investigator]] that a television network hired in the course of a [[due diligence]] investigation, Wattenburg admitted utilizing such environmentally destructive mining practices. The investigator reported:

{{cquote|"The first task was to cut 2,000,000 tons of 'overburden' dirt and rock off the top of the mountain and move it a half mile away, where it was dumped into a deep canyon. Overburden is the dirt and rock on top of the ore body beneath it. The gold ore body was at a depth of two hundred feet below the surface&nbsp;... Here is how one seasoned operator described it: '...&nbsp;he put maybe five or six of us on bulldozers to start pushing dirt on the mountaintop into this trench, up at the top of the trench. Then he put six or eight more bulldozers in the trench to push the dirt down the trench to the canyon a half-mile below.' "<ref name="Pushback.com">{{cite web | url= http://www.pushback.com/Wattenburg/bio/GoldMine.html | title = Bill Wattenburg's Background: The Gold Mine}}
</ref>}}

== Radio talk show host ==
From 1972 to December 2, 2011, Wattenburg was the host of ''The Open Line to the West Coast'', a talk show heard late Saturday and Sunday evenings 10 p.m. to 1 a.m. [[Pacific Time Zone|PT]] from San Francisco on [[KGO (AM)|KGO]], [[Medium wave|AM]] 810&nbsp;kHz.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kgoam810.com/programschedule.asp |title=KGO's Program Schedule |access-date=2011-12-10 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111106132728/http://www.kgoam810.com/programschedule.asp |archivedate=2011-11-06 }}</ref> On the program, Wattenburg took calls from throughout the western United States. Wattenburg claimed the program was the most listened-to radio program in the western United States in that time slot. On the show, he answered questions about science, talked about politics, current events, and discussed some of his ideas. Some of his recurring topics were whether [[Gasoline#Octane rating|premium gasoline]] was worthwhile, [[nuclear power]], and [[Environmental movement#Criticisms|criticism of the environmental movement]]. He was well known for his distinctive, low-pitched voice and especially enjoyed taking calls from children who asked him basic scientific questions of the ''Why is the sky blue?'' variety. Wattenburg was fired by KGO, along with most of the station's other talk hosts on December 2, 2011, as the station, owned by [[Cumulus Media]] decided to abandon the long-time and listener-appreciated talk radio format and switch to a mostly news format in competition with #1 [[KCBS (AM)|KCBS]].<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.sfgate.com/bayarea/matier-ross/article/kgo-radio-going-to-news-format-veterans-leaving-2344387.php | work=The San Francisco Chronicle | first1=Phillip | last1=Matier | first2=Andrew | last2=Ross | title=KGO radio going to news format&nbsp;— veterans leaving | date=2 December 2011}}</ref> KGO's website showed his former time slot would be replaced with Spencer Hughes.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kgoradio.com/programschedule.asp |title=KGO Newstalk 810 San Francisco |access-date=2011-12-03 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111126094132/http://kgoradio.com/programschedule.asp |archivedate=2011-11-26 }}</ref>

In late 2011, Wattenburg began broadcasting on [[KSCO]]-AM, 1080, Santa Cruz, California. This was a few days after parting ways with KGO-AM. This continued until January 22, 2012, when he joined the Talk Radio Network<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trn1.com/wattenburg-about| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120511053807/http://www.trn1.com/wattenburg-about | archive-date=2012-05-11 | title=The Bill Wattenburg Show | access-date=2023-11-08}}</ref>

In 2012, Bill Wattenburg signed with Talk Radio Network and his show was available to radio stations nationwide in syndication.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.trn1.com/dr-bill-wattenburg-joins-trn-entertainment | title=Dr. Bill Wattenburg Joins TRN Entertainment Bringing a Wealth of Practical Science to Radio | date=2012-01-12}}</ref> His program was called ''The Open Line to America''. Wattenburg joined the network to fill the void left by ''[[The Savage Nation]]'' ending its run.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/09/28/michael-savage-talk-radio-network_n_1923066.html | title=HuffPost - Breaking News, U.S. And World News | website=[[HuffPost]] }}</ref> The program aired Sunday nights from 8 p.m. to 11 p.m. Pacific Time. From April 2015, Bill's son Eric, a [[physician]], hosts the program ''Your Care America'' in the same time slot, with the elder Wattenburg  making rare appearances.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.talkradionetwork.com/shows/your-care-america/|title=Your Care America with Dr. Eric Wattenburg&nbsp;— Talk Radio Network|newspaper=Talk Radio Network|publisher=|archive-date=2016-08-31|access-date=2016-08-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160831054911/http://www.talkradionetwork.com/shows/your-care-america/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://fth.stparchive.com/Archive/FTH/FTH04222015P06.php|title=Feather River Bulletin April 22 Page 6|publisher=}}</ref>

== Political views ==
He was generally considered a [[Conservatism|conservative]]; however, he espoused some traditionally [[Modern liberalism in the United States|liberal]] or [[Libertarianism|libertarian]] positions on a handful of social issues, such as [[Abortion-rights movements|abortion rights]]. He was a strong supporter of former [[Governor of California]] [[Arnold Schwarzenegger]], as well as former president [[George W. Bush]] and the [[Iraq War|invasion and occupation of Iraq]].

For example, Wattenburg long railed against the use of [[Methyl tert-butyl ether|MTBE]], a chemical industry waste product added to gasoline for the purpose of minimizing pollutants from automobiles, but which sometimes polluted groundwater. Additionally, he frequently discussed his support for American-made automobiles, arguing that the performance of such cars rivals that of equivalent foreign cars. A longtime consultant at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]], Wattenburg expressed strong support for nuclear power and anger at the [[Sierra Club]] and the [[environmentalism|environmental movement]], as well as other public interest groups such [[Consumers Union]] for their opposition to nuclear power.

=== Firearms confiscation ===
Wattenburg openly suggested having [[standing army|standing armies]] on American streets and within American homes for law enforcement purposes, once remarking to a ''San Francisco Chronicle'' reporter, in regard to high urban violence in Oakland, California, "Our troops are going house to house removing weapons in Bosnia. Why not use them to do that in West Oakland or South Central Los Angeles?"<ref>{{cite news
| url = https://www.sfgate.com/politics/joegarofoli/article/CHRONICLE-PROFILE-Bill-Wattenburg-Radio-host-2787327.php
| title = Chronicle Profile: Bill Wattenburg, Radio host keeps creative lines open; Inventor, best-selling author creates simple solutions to complex problems
| work = San Francisco Chronicle
| author = Joe Garofoli, Chronicle Staff Writer
| date = 7 October 2002
| access-date = 6 June 2009
}}</ref>

==Author==
As an author, Wattenburg published two books for the general public: one book, ''Best Jokes From Talk Radio'', is a compilation of risque jokes heard on talk radio; his second book, ''How to Find and Fascinate a Mistress'', is a fictionalized version of Wattenburg's exploits with young women in the 1970s. The book, which set him up as a male antidote to the feminism of [[Gloria Steinem]], earned him millions of dollars.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} It was published under the [[pseudonym]] ''Will Harvey.'' The book has long been out of print.

==Marriage and family==
Wattenburg was married to his third spouse, Carol Wattenburg, 28 years his junior.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Garofoli|first=Joe|date=2002-10-07|title=CHRONICLE PROFILE / Bill Wattenburg / Radio host keeps creative lines open / Inventor, best-selling author creates simple solutions to complex problems|url=https://www.sfgate.com/politics/joegarofoli/article/CHRONICLE-PROFILE-Bill-Wattenburg-Radio-host-2787327.php|access-date=2021-12-19|website=SFGATE|language=en-US}}</ref> They had two daughters; Wattenburg also had three children from a previous marriage.<ref name=":0" />

==Appearance in films==
Wattenburg made brief appearances in three [[Clint Eastwood]] films: ''[[The Dead Pool]]'' (Nolan Kennard), ''[[Pink Cadillac (film)|Pink Cadillac]]'' (pit boss), and ''[[True Crime (1999 film)|True Crime]]'' (radio reporter).
